name: – Li Andersson – Amendments by the committee responsible – separate votes – Am 18/2
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the Member States
part_text: Member States should foster equal opportunities for all by addressing inequalities in education and training, including territorial disparities in access, through high-quality, universal accessible and affordable education. Children, regardless of their families’ economic situation, should be provided with access to affordable and high quality early childhood education and care, in line with the “Barcelona targets” and the European Child Guarantee. Member States should raise overall qualification levels, reduce the number of early leavers from education and training, support equal access to education for children from disadvantaged groups and remote areas, including Roma children. They should also increase the attractiveness, quality and labour market relevance of vocational education and training (VET), promote VET as an equal and valued pathway alongside academic pathways within their education and training systems. They should also support access to and completion of tertiary education, and increase the number of science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) graduates both in VET and in tertiary education, especially women. Member States should take targeted action to close the gender gap in digital and AI skills and in STEM career pathways, from early education through to reskilling programmes. Top performance and excellence in educational outcomes should also be supported, given their role in fostering the future innovation potential of the Union and competitiveness. Member States should facilitate the transition from education to employment for young people through paid, accessible and quality traineeships and apprenticeships, as well as counselling, and increase participation of adults in learning, particularly among learners from disadvantaged backgrounds and those with fewer opportunities to engage in learning. Quality traineeships should require a written agreement before the traineeship begins, specifying its duration, remuneration, learning objectives, rights and duties and mentoring arrangements. Trainees should receive fair remuneration, social protection and equal treatment. Member States should upgrade and increase the supply and uptake of flexible initial and continuing VET, and strengthen work-based learning in VET systems, while ensuring sufficient in-person teaching and adequate teacher-student ratios at VET institutions. Member States should support the development and strengthening of regional Centres of Vocational Excellence initiatives, including through cooperation between VET providers, enterprises, social partners, public authorities and other relevant stakeholders, as platforms for excellence, innovation, skills development and technology transfer. Furthermore, Member States should enhance the labour market relevance of tertiary education and, where appropriate, research; improve skills intelligence; make skills and qualifications more visible, transferable and comparable, including those acquired abroad, and ensure a more consistent use of EU-wide classifications (i.e. ESCO); increase opportunities for validating and recognising skills and competences acquired outside formal education and training, and promote faster recognition of qualifications for Union and third-country nationals, while maintaining quality standards.
